body:
# README writing guidelines (Filemark)

Rules for the public `README.md` at `github.com/thesatellite-ai/filemark`.
Purpose: keep the README user-facing, SEO-strong, and on-brand. Every
change to the README should pass these rules.

---

## 1. Audience

Writing for one persona:

- A developer or technical writer who reads a lot of markdown / JSON /
  schemas in the browser
- Landed here from a Google search, the Chrome Web Store listing, or a
  shared link
- Wants to know in 10 seconds: *what does this do, why should I care,
  how do I install it*
- Probably never heard of us

Not writing for: contributors, plugin authors, internal engineers.
Those docs live separately in the private repo.

---

## 2. Tone

- **Confident, not humble.** "The best markdown viewer for Chrome" beats
  "a nice markdown viewer".
- **Opinionated, not neutral.** Pick fights with obvious pain points
  ("every existing viewer is stuck in 2018").
- **Specific, not vague.** "Full-text search across every loaded file in
  under 100 ms" beats "fast search".
- **No corporate voice.** Avoid "our solution", "best-in-class",
  "empower users". Write like a trusted friend recommending the tool.
- **No apology language.** No "this is early", "still rough",
  "contributions welcome to polish". Readers should feel they're
  getting a finished product.

---

## 3. Positioning

Three non-negotiable framings:

1. **Multi-format, not just markdown.** Mention MD, MDX, JSON, JSONC,
   SQL, Prisma, DBML in the H1 and the lead paragraph.
2. **Built out of frustration.** The "why" section exists to say
   competitors are abandoned / buggy / MV2 / stripped down. Name the
   gap, not the competitors.
3. **Local-first and private.** Lead with "100% on your machine, no
   cloud, no account, no tracking". It's a wedge against SaaS viewers.

---

## 4. Section order (locked)

The public README ships in this order. Do not reshuffle without reason:

1. H1 + elevator pitch blockquote
2. One-paragraph hook emphasizing pain + positioning
3. One-line closing punch ("This is the file reader Chrome should have
   shipped with.")
4. Table of contents
5. **Why Filemark** — the frustration pitch
6. **What you can open** — the format table
7. **Features that other viewers can't touch** — grouped benefits
8. **Install** — from source (until Web Store ships)
9. **Usage** — the three entry points
10. **Custom components in markdown**
11. **Keyboard shortcuts**
12. **Options & customization**
13. **Auto-refresh / Tabs / URL sync** (inline blocks)
14. **How Filemark compares** — the comparison table
15. **Build from source** — for contributors; keep short
16. **FAQ**
17. **Roadmap**

Sections NOT to include:

- ❌ Credits / Acknowledgments
- ❌ License (keep `LICENSE` file at repo root; GitHub surfaces it)
- ❌ Contributing (source-available license; feedback goes via Issues)
- ❌ Architecture / Tech stack sections
- ❌ Changelog (use GitHub Releases)

---

## 5. What to include in feature copy

Every feature bullet should answer *"what do I get"* — never *"what is
it built with"*. Rewrite examples:

| ❌ Bad | ✅ Good |
|---|---|
| "Rendered with `react-markdown` and `remark-gfm`" | "Full GitHub-flavored rendering — tables, task lists, math" |
| "Uses `@uiw/react-json-view` under the hood" | "A real, interactive JSON tree. Collapse, expand, copy" |
| "SQL parser via `db-schema-toolkit`" | "Drop any Postgres, MySQL, or SQLite schema — get an interactive ER diagram" |
| "KaTeX for math" | "Math — inline and block, with a typesetter as good as academic papers" |
| "Shiki for syntax highlighting" | "Syntax-highlighted code blocks in 30+ languages" |
| "MV3 with no `unsafe-eval`" | "Hardened against the strictest Chrome content-security policy" |

The full tech stack lives in the private `ARCHITECTURE.md`. The public
README acknowledges *zero* library names in the feature body. A single
link to `@maxgfr` is acceptable in a dedicated spot if ever reinstated
— but by default, no.

---

## 6. SEO principles

The README is indexed; treat it as a landing page.

- **H1** must include the primary keywords: "Markdown", "JSON", the
  key formats, and "Chrome"
- **Lead paragraph** (first 160 chars) should be copy-pasteable as the
  meta description
- **H2s** should read as natural-search phrases — "How Filemark
  compares", "What you can open"
- **Tables** are gold — Google lifts them into rich snippets
- **FAQs** feed "People also ask"
- **External links** only to authoritative sources (CommonMark spec,
  GFM spec, major libraries we want associated with the product)
- **Internal links** use the slugified H2 headings; keep them
  lowercase-hyphenated
- **Images**, when added, need descriptive alt text and the extension
  filename (e.g. `filemark-screenshot-dark.png`)

---

## 7. Framing rules for specific sections

### Why Filemark

Lead with competitor failure modes (bullet list of what "most
extensions" lack). Don't name brands. Close with a single "Filemark was
built because …" sentence.

### Format table

Columns: Format · Extensions · What you get. The "What you get" column
is benefit-framed — same rules as § 5.

### Features section

Four grouped subsections:

1. **Rendering that actually works** — the renderer side
2. **A real library, not just a file dropper** — tabs, folders,
   search
3. **UI that respects your screen** — theming, fullscreen,
   deep-linking
4. **Privacy and performance you can audit** — MV3, local-first,
   security
5. **Built to be configured, not to annoy** — options page

If a new group is added, keep it benefit-framed and defend the name
against "ships with X" phrasing.

### Comparison table

Always 5 columns: `Filemark`, `Most markdown extensions`, `Online
viewers`, `Obsidian / VS Code`. Keep the row order stable; add new
rows at the bottom. Use ✅ / ⚠️ / ❌ / — only — no text explanations
per cell.

### FAQ

Questions the actual user would ask, not questions the engineer would
love to answer. Examples of good questions:

- "Is any of my data sent anywhere?"
- "Does it work offline?"
- "Will it replace VS Code / Obsidian?"
- "What about security?"

Examples of bad questions (leave for ARCHITECTURE.md):

- "How does the MDX pipeline work?"
- "Why didn't you use `@mdx-js/mdx` `evaluate()`?"

---

## 8. Word choices to keep / avoid

**Preferred words**: beautifully, instantly, local-first,
copy-pasteable, hardened, distraction-free, every edge case, real
(as in "a real tree, not a prettified blob").

**Banned / cringe**: best-in-class, enterprise-grade, revolutionary,
empower, seamlessly, unleash, next-generation, AI-powered (unless
actually AI), ecosystem, synergy.

**Don't pair**: "powerful" + "simple" ("simple yet powerful" is
cliché).

---

## 9. Source-available framing

We are source-available, not open source. The README should:

- Never say "open source" as a standalone claim
- Close the footer with a neutral phrase ("The Satellite AI", not
  "open source")
- Rely on the `LICENSE` file at the repo root for the legal terms —
  don't restate them in the README

GitHub auto-displays a "View license" link in the sidebar; that's
enough.

---

## 10. Maintenance rules

- **When a feature ships**, update the feature table + the comparison
  table in the same PR. Don't let them drift.
- **When a format lands**, update the H1, the lead paragraph, the
  format table, the options-page bullet, and the Roadmap (remove the
  item).
- **Screenshots**: keep under 3. One dark, one light, one with a
  schema diagram. Store them in `apps/chrome-ext/public/marketing/`
  and reference with relative paths that also work on the Chrome Web
  Store listing.
- **Reading time**: the README should stay under a 6-minute read.
  Prune aggressively. Split to docs/ if something grows past its
  section weight.
- **Punchiness budget**: no more than one superlative ("best",
  "fastest", "only") per H2 section. Overuse feels spammy.

---

## 11. Pre-publish checklist

Before merging a README change, verify:

- [ ] H1 still contains: Markdown · MDX · JSON · (plus whatever new
      format) · Chrome
- [ ] Zero library / package names in the feature body
- [ ] All internal anchors resolve (run the TOC)
- [ ] No "open source" claim anywhere
- [ ] Comparison table still has 15 rows (add at bottom, never remove)
- [ ] Roadmap pruned of anything shipped
- [ ] Footer tagline unchanged unless intentional
- [ ] Word count under ~2,500 (currently ≈ 2,200)
